title: Low-friction embedded SDK sprint: playpen notes (draft)
body:
Goal:
Run a short sprint (3 days) to prototype a low-friction embedded SDK experience for product teams who want a lightweight client that can be dropped into frontends and mobile apps. Focus on first-10-minutes success: minimal install, clear telemetry, obvious fallback behavior, and a tiny sample app showing offline-first + Redwood hosted fallback.

Audience:
- Engineering teams integrating small LLM features into existing apps (search augmentation, short-form assistants, autofill).
- Solutions engineers doing quick PoCs for customers.

Hypotheses to validate (ranked):
1) A single small artifact (npm + 1 small prebuilt wasm bundle) plus 4-line init code will get >50% of internal devs from zero to sample in <10 minutes.
2) Telemetry that surfaces per-request latency + token cost in dev mode will drastically reduce integration churn.
3) A clear local-first failover (local stub -> local LLM sim -> hosted Redwood) reduces time-to-demo and incident tickets.

Sprint outline (3-day playpen):
Day 0 (prep):
- pick 2 sample integrations: Search-autocomplete widget + support-chat mini assistant
- agree on minimal API shape: createClient({apiKey, mode}) and client.generate(prompt, opts)
- choose telemetry fields (see telemetry contract below)

Day 1 (default dev flow):
- implement tiny npm package (index.js) that wraps fetch/WS to Redwood, includes an ember-friendly browser drop-in and React hook.
- deliver a prebuilt wasm stub (100–300KB) that simulates latency and returns canned completions for offline demos.
- add quickstart README, 2-lines to copy-paste into product sandbox.

Day 2 (ops & telemetry):
- wire a dev-mode telemetry endpoint (local only) that logs latency, token_estimate, model_name, fallback_used.
- add a small UI overlay (dev flag) that surfaces these metrics in the sample apps.
- run 3 internal devs through the path and time them.

Experiment matrix (minimal):
- Variant A: default client + wasm stub (no telemetry)
- Variant B: client + wasm stub + inline dev telemetry overlay
- Variant C: client + explicit fallback policies exposed in config (retry/backoff)
Metrics to capture:
- time_to_first_completion (measured in minutes)
- number_of_help_tickets_from_demo_sessions (qualitative)
- dev-reported friction points (post-run notes)

Telemetry contract (dev-mode):
- event: request_sent -> {timestamp_iso, request_id, client_version, model_hint}
- event: response_received -> {timestamp_iso, request_id, latency_ms, token_estimate, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_name, fallback_flag}
- event: error -> {timestamp_iso, request_id, error_code, retry_count, last_fallback}
(note: strip PII; only send ephemeral request_id in dev mode — we will never send prompt text in dev telemetry)

Minimal API sketch (copyable):
// install: npm i @redwood/embed-sdk
// usage:
// import {createClient} from '@redwood/embed-sdk'
// const client = createClient({ apiKey: 'DEV_KEY', mode: 'dev' })
// const r = await client.generate('summarize: \n//    - keep it as short as possible', {maxTokens: 80})
// r.text -> completion text

Failure modes & fallbacks (design notes):
- Local stub unavailable: show inline error with "Run local dev stub (npm run start-stub)" and fallback to hosted disabled by default for security.
- Hosted rate limit: automatically switch to lower-cost compact model_hint and surface that change in telemetry overlay.
- High latency: for UI widgets use streaming token-by-token display; otherwise present a partial placeholder and retry policy.

Checklists (for a minimal internal alpha release):
- [ ] small npm package + Readme + 2 sample apps (React + plain HTML)
- [ ] wasm stub and npm script to run it locally
- [ ] telemetry dev overlay and contract implemented
- [ ] a one-page quickstart copy for SEs (two screenshots, three bullets)
- [ ] short internal playbook for debugging common failures

Open questions (to resolve during sprint):
- Auth: do we standardize on apiKey-as-header for dev keys, or provide opt-in OAuth for SEs embedding demos?
- Telemetry hygiene: where do dev-mode telemetry logs land long term (kinesis/dev cluster vs ephemeral file)?
- Size targets: can we get the wasm stub <200KB gzipped? if not, what's acceptable for mobile quickstarts?

Next steps after sprint (if success):
- move package to monorepo, CI + smoke tests (local stub smoke + hosted connectivity), publish internal npm tag.
- draft a short SE playbook and a 10-min demo script for Enablement.
- track DEVEXP-278 for follow-up items (auth, size optimizations, and mobile packaging).

Notes to self / quick reminders:
- keep surface minimal — devs hate config. 3 sensible defaults > 10 knobs.
- avoid sending any prompt text in telemetry. always token_estimate not token_text.
- demo first in a very small sample app (search with 3 results) — wins demos quickly.

Raw scribbles / fragments (copy-pasteable bits):
- "createClient({apiKey, mode='dev', fallback: {strategy: 'hosted-if-allowed'}})"
- spawn-local-stub: npm run dev-stub -> serves wasm + tiny JSON file mapping prompts to canned responses
- test plan: 6 internal devs (non-SE) run quickstart, capture time-to-first-success + subjective NPS"
